technical_body.trigger: STA associates to any AP in a Mobility Domain for the first time
technical_body.keying: runs a normal 4-way handshake; derives PMK-R0 (per mobility domain) and PMK-R1 (per BSSID)
artifacts: MDE (IE 54) in beacon confirms FT capability

technical_body.trigger: STA moves to a new AP in the same MD
technical_body.shape: single Reassoc Request/Response pair carries the FTE
attack_surface: KRACK CVE-2017-13082 replays this to reinstall PTK

technical_body.trigger: STA sends Neighbor Report Request; AP responds with list of preferred neighbor BSSIDs
attack_surface: spoofed Neighbor Report steers STA toward rogue BSSID

technical_body.trigger: AP sends BTM Request (WNM Action, category 10, action 7) suggesting STA move to a specific BSSID
technical_body.response: BTM Response with accepted/reject status code
attack_surface: crafted BTM Request from a rogue shoves the STA onto attacker BSSID

technical_body.trigger: STA sends GAS Initial Request with ANQP query IDs; AP responds
technical_body.shape: Action frames (Category 4 Public Action, Action 10=GAS Initial Request / 11=GAS Initial Response)
attack_surface: Realm/Domain string exfil from a puzzle AP

technical_body.trigger: STA with Passpoint profile finds an OSU-advertising AP
technical_body.flow: OSU Server URL from ANQP → HTTPS enrollment → provisioned Passpoint profile
attack_surface: rogue OSU server phishes provisioning credentials

technical_body.trigger: STA sends FT Request via the current AP (over-the-DS) rather than to the target AP directly
technical_body.use: Client cannot yet tune the target AP's channel — controller-mediated roam

technical_body.trigger: STA reassociates to an AP it has already 4-way'd with; presents the PMKID to skip full auth
technical_body.artifact: PMKID in the RSN IE — the value Steube 2018 recovers

technical_body.note: Vendor-proprietary extension of PMKSA caching to share PMK across APs in the same fleet; superseded by 11r for standards-based deployments

technical_body.role: AP suppresses 2.4 GHz probe responses to dual-band clients to nudge them to 5 GHz
technical_body.attack: Deliberately jam or spoof congestion on 5 GHz to force clients back to attacker-controlled 2.4 GHz

technical_body.note: Controller-based steering that rejects new associations to overloaded APs — clients try neighbors; attacker BSSID that appears less loaded gets preferred.

technical_body.returns: list of NAI Realms + EAP methods supported. Per IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 9-271: ANQP element 264 = NAI Realm.
list of Venue Name entries with language codes. Per IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 9-271: ANQP element 259 = Venue Name.
PLMN list — the mobile carrier IDs the AP offloads for. Per IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 9-271: ANQP element 265 = 3GPP Cellular Network.
AP's DNS domain name. Per IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 9-271: ANQP element 269 = Domain Name.
list of Roaming Consortium OIs (3-15 bytes each). Per IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 9-271: ANQP element 262 = Roaming Consortium.

technical_body.role: R0KH (holds PMK-R0) and R1KH (holds PMK-R1) roles among APs in an 11r mobility domain; controller-mediated for enterprise fleets
technical_body.attack_surface: misconfigured deployments share PMK-R0 across BSSIDs — see ft-r0-shared-fleet-crack
